text: To simulate something is to copy it as practice. NASA will simulate a trip to Mars here on Earth.
A participant is a person who takes part in something. These four people will join the practice mission.
A habitat is a place where someone lives. A Mars habitat is a building where people could live on Mars.
NASA is the group in the United States that sends rockets and astronauts into space.
Mars is a red planet. It is far away from Earth.
A mission is a special job or trip with a goal.
Simulated means copied as practice. It is not the real thing.
Seeking means looking for something.
This is the name of the practice mission. An analog is a copy of something real, used for practice.
A press release is a short note that tells news writers about something new.
Astronauts are people who travel into space.
Deep space means very far away from Earth, past the moon.
This is a NASA place in Texas. Astronauts train and get help from people there.
Houston is a big city in the state of Texas.
Facilities are buildings made for a special use.
The interior is the inside of something.
A spacecraft is a vehicle that travels in space.
A real spacewalk is when an astronaut floats outside a spacecraft. A virtual one is pretend, done with computers.
A delay is waiting. Far away in space, messages take a long time to get home.
This is a NASA team. It studies how space travel changes people’s bodies and minds.
TFK is short for TIME for Kids, the magazine that wrote this article.
Habitation means living in a place.
Here, translate means to take what you learned in one place and use it in another.
An emergency is a sudden problem that needs help right away.
Supplies are things people need, like food and water.
Data is information that people collect to learn something.
Recruits are people who are chosen to join a group.
